description:
At the end of the day, the most important question in a relationship is simple:

Do they feel like home?

If you’ve got that - plus loyalty, kindness, and someone who treats people well - you’ve hit the jackpot.

Everything else? Those are just skills. And skills can be learned.

No one comes fully baked. We all grow, learn, and evolve together, and that’s what makes love (and life) so beautiful.

Thank you, @brookemiccio and @daniellecarolan, for having me on @galsonthegopodcast! I had the best time chatting with you both about all things Let Them and so much more 💚

🎧 Listen now: “listen to this if you’re in your 20s!!! with MEL ROBBINS”
transcript: The most important things in a relationship, I say this to our kids who are 26, 25, and 20, do they feel like home? Can you walk through the door and exhale? You know like when you play tag as a kid and there's a safe base? Yeah. That's your partner. And so if you've got 80% of the right things, which are, are they loyal? Do you feel like they're home? Do your shoulders drop and you exhale? When you get a text are you like oh that's my person you know when do they have lifelong friends do they have good relationships with family like do they treat people well when you're out if you got that you've hit the jackpot everything else in life is a skill and somebody can learn it and if they don't have it like talk about it like oh my god that made me cry no it's so and it's true about friends too it's just like everyone in your life 80 percent like they're yeah yeah and and there was somebody that came on our podcast dr stewart ablon that said this thing that I wish I had known decades before. He's a psychologist at Mass General Brigham, the number one research hospital in the world. And he specializes in clinical psychology with kids. And he said, kids do well when they can. And if somebody's challenging, it's because they're missing a skill. That's it. And I believe all people do well when they can. Yeah. And that people want to do well and they want to succeed in the relationship. And so, like, stop annihilating people because they don't have the skills that you're expecting. So anybody can learn how to make a bed. Anybody can learn how to cook. Anybody can learn how to fold clothes and do laundry. Anybody can learn how to enjoy nicer meals and nicer restaurants. Anybody can learn how to get in better shape. Anybody can learn how to have a budget. You know, I also say this to our daughters. You guys idolize your dad. He's 29 years in the making, okay? Like, okay, When I got him at the age of 25 here in New York City, that is not the man that you see now. He was a wonderful person with all the 80%. Yeah. But he was the youngest of three boys. Like, he had a lot of skills to build. Right. But he's a guy that wanted to learn and wanted to grow. And they don't your person shouldn't come fully baked but if you got the right ingredients you can make something amazing
